summary:
Sprinklers is a web app that turns two decades of NASA satellite fire detections into one consistent burning calendar. MODIS (since 2000, 1 km pixels) and VIIRS (since 2012, 375 m pixels) detect fires at different resolutions, so their raw counts cannot be compared directly. We built a pipeline on NASA FIRMS data that filters low-confidence and static heat sources, aggregates detections onto a common ~1 km grid, and calibrates MODIS against VIIRS over their overlap years. The result is a continuous, VIIRS-equivalent record from 2000 to today, with no visible break at the sensor transition.

Users search any place on a 3D globe, choose a radius and period, and see a year × month calendar, anomalies against the historical median, rankings and CSV/PNG exports, without choosing a sensor.

This directly addresses the challenge of harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS hot spots. It matters because emergency managers, land managers and scientists can finally tell whether a fire season is truly above normal, using open NASA data.

details: Sprinklers is a web app that turns two decades of NASA satellite fire detections into one consistent burning calendar. The two sensors count fires differently: MODIS (since 2000) has 1 km pixels, and VIIRS (since 2012) has 375 m pixels. Their raw counts cannot be compared directly. Our pipeline cleans NASA FIRMS hotspots by confidence level and removes static heat sources such as gas flares and industry. It then places the detections on a regular grid of about 1 km and counts “fire cell-days”, so both sensors use the same unit and duplicates between satellites are handled. It calibrates MODIS against VIIRS over the years when both were flying, which gives a VIIRS-equivalent record from 2000 to today. The user searches a place or types coordinates, sets a radius and a period, and gets a year × month calendar. The app also shows anomalies against the historical median, rankings, a seasonal profile and a hotspot map, and exports to CSV, PNG and SVG. The user never has to choose a sensor.
